text: Imagine a stock that has climbed for months, from thirty two dollars all the way to sixty.
visual: Price chart on real axes (day, price $); line draws up from 32 to 60.

text: It dips, then pushes to a new high of seventy.
visual: Line dips to 52, climbs to 70; '70' tag pops.

text: But the next push only reaches sixty one. It could not even make a new high.
visual: Line dips to 52, climbs to 61; dashed line from 70 shows the gap; 'lower high' chip.

text: Then it falls through a level it had bounced off twice before.
visual: Two bounce points at 52 pulse; the line breaks below 52.

text: Traders have a name for this shape. It looks like a person: two shoulders and a head.
visual: Silhouette of a head and shoulders fades in over the three peaks.

text: The head and shoulders pattern.
visual: Title card: HEAD & SHOULDERS PATTERN / explained simply, with real numbers.

text: Welcome to Math Lab TV. Where math is something you can see.
visual: Logo + MATH LAB TV + tagline.

text: Today you will learn how to spot the three peaks.
visual: ① mini three-peak line; 'spot the three peaks'.

text: You will see why the neckline is the line that matters.
visual: ② mini chart with yellow neckline; 'the neckline'.

text: And you will measure a price target with simple subtraction.
Let's slow down and read the chart one peak at a time.
visual: Full chart; camera zooms to the first peak.

text: The first peak, at sixty, is the left shoulder. Buyers are still in control.
visual: Blue marker 'left shoulder 60'.

text: The second peak, at seventy, is the head. It is the highest point of the whole move.
visual: Orange marker 'head 70'.

text: The third peak, at sixty one, is the right shoulder. It is lower than the head.
visual: Blue marker 'right shoulder 61'; arrow 70 → 61 labelled 'lower high'.

text: That lower high is the first warning. Buyers tried again, and they ran out of strength.
visual: Up-arrows shrinking: +18, then +9.

text: The shoulders do not need to match exactly. Real charts are never that neat.
visual: Left and right shoulder bars side by side: 60 vs 61 'close enough'.

text: Now look at the two dips between the peaks. Both stopped at fifty two.
visual: Two dots at the troughs, labelled 52.

text: Join them with a line, and you have the neckline.
visual: Yellow neckline drawn through both dips.

text: Here is the key idea. Until price closes below the neckline, there is no pattern yet.
visual: Line beyond the right shoulder fades to grey; 'not confirmed' chip.

text: It is only a shape that might become one.
visual: Ghost path that bounces off 52 and goes back up.

text: When the price closes below fifty two, the pattern is confirmed.
visual: Line closes below 52; 'confirmed' chip turns yellow.

text: Volume often tells the same story. Trading is lighter on the right shoulder, then jumps on the break.
visual: Aqua volume bars under the chart: smaller at right shoulder, tall bar at the break.

text: And sometimes the price comes back up to touch the neckline from below, before it falls away.
visual: Pullback to 53 marked 'retest'; old floor now acts as a ceiling.

text: So how far might it fall? There is a simple rule of thumb.
visual: Chart; violet ruler appears.

text: Measure the height of the head above the neckline.
visual: Vertical violet bracket from 52 to 70.

text: Seventy minus fifty two is eighteen dollars.
visual: 70 − 52 = 18 written beside the bracket.

text: Now copy that same eighteen down from the neckline.
visual: Bracket slides down below 52.

text: Fifty two minus eighteen is thirty four. That is the price target.
visual: 52 − 18 = 34; violet dashed target line at 34.

text: Traders also decide where they would be wrong. A common choice is just above the right shoulder, at sixty one.
visual: Red stop line at 61.

text: Selling at the break, at fifty two, risks nine dollars to aim for eighteen.
visual: Red bar 9 (risk) vs violet bar 18 (reward).

text: That is two dollars of possible reward for every dollar of risk.
visual: '2 : 1' badge.

text: Three mistakes trip up beginners.
visual: Three cards appear.

text: Mistake one: acting before the neckline breaks. Many right shoulders simply turn back up.
visual: Card 1, red: ghost path bounces off the neckline.

text: Mistake two: finding the shape anywhere. It is a reversal pattern, so it needs an uptrend before it to reverse.
visual: Card 2: same shape inside a downtrend, crossed out.

text: Mistake three: treating the target as a promise. It is a rule of thumb. Price can stop short, or overshoot.
visual: Card 3: target line with arrows above and below it.

text: And a bonus: flip the chart upside down, and you get the inverse head and shoulders, a possible bottom after a fall.
visual: Chart flips vertically; label 'inverse head and shoulders'.

text: Here is the whole recipe.
visual: Numbered card appears.

text: One. Start with an uptrend.
visual: Step 1 lights up.

text: Two. Find three peaks, with the head the highest.
visual: Step 2.

text: Three. Draw the neckline through the two dips.
visual: Step 3.

text: Four. Wait for a close below it.
visual: Step 4.

text: Five. Measure the head, copy it down, and set where you would be wrong.
visual: Step 5.

text: A pattern is not a prediction. It is a way to plan your risk.
visual: Closing line in violet.

text: Look around your world, and notice how often a rally runs out of steam before it turns.
visual: Four cards: stock chart, house prices, a sports streak, a viral trend; stamp 'lower high?'.

text: If this lesson made things clear for you, please subscribe to Math Lab TV, so we can keep building together.
visual: Logo + SUBSCRIBE button clicked.

text: But here's a puzzle for next time.
visual: Small logo top-centre; puzzle icon.

text: What if the price makes only two peaks, at the same height? That is the double top.
visual: Mini chart with two equal peaks; 'next: double top' chip.
